subject.title: Export installed agents as grouped Claw packages

question: Should experimental Claw export require complete, exact recorded state by default, with any drifted export deferred to an explicit snapshot mode, before this stacked feature is accepted?
rationale: This choice defines the meaning, portability guarantees, and recovery behavior of a newly introduced package-export contract; tests cannot decide whether partial local state should be refused or intentionally serialized as a snapshot.

options.title: Adopt exact-state export
options.body: Keep the current fail-closed export behavior, require current-head proof for both the successful round trip and drift rejection, and stage it after its lifecycle prerequisite.

options.title: Design snapshot mode
options.body: Add an explicitly named snapshot mode with a machine-readable drift report and lineage metadata instead of treating incomplete state as a normal export.

options.title: Pause export scope
options.body: Defer export until the Claws lifecycle and canonical manifest format are accepted as a cohesive product direction.

recommendation.title: Adopt exact-state export
recommendation.body: Keep the current fail-closed export behavior, require current-head proof for both the successful round trip and drift rejection, and stage it after its lifecycle prerequisite.

likelyOwner.reason: The contributor has authored the connected lifecycle/export stack and can provide the most concrete contract and implementation context, though final product acceptance remains a maintainer decision.
